requirements.requirement: node1 given a routed address on each of its two segments (seg-a via eth1, seg-b via eth2)
requirements.summary: eth1 assigned 192.168.11.1/24 and eth2 assigned 192.168.12.1/24 on node1, confirmed via ip -4 addr and ip route showing both subnets directly connected.

requirements.requirement: Working path between node2 and node3 (routed through node1)
requirements.summary: node2 and node3 given static addresses/routes on their eth1 interfaces via node1; bidirectional ping succeeded across the 192.168.11.0/24 <-> 192.168.12.0/24 segments through node1 with ip_forward enabled.

requirements.requirement: Configuration on node1 returns automatically after node1 is restarted, with node2<->node3 reachability restored
requirements.summary: After three failed persistence attempts (manual ifup not surviving reboot; then a periodic SONiC reconciler stripping static addresses within ~1 minute of boot), a self-healing systemd watchdog (Restart=always, 5s loop) was installed. The final validated restart cycle shows: pre-restart boot_id ee788f65..., reboot acknowledgement, changed boot_id 66411cad... confirming an actual reboot, and post-reboot eth1/eth2 addressing, forwarding sysctls, and node2<->node3 ping all recovered automatically and remained stable across repeated checks.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node1 received routed addresses on both segments, node2 and node3 achieved a working end-to-end path through node1, and — critically — the configuration was demonstrated to return automatically after a node1 restart, with a full pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery of addressing, forwarding, and node2<->node3 connectivity all directly observed in the final validated restart cycle. The executor also completed the provider-wide restart protocol on node2 and node3, each showing consistent baseline/ack/changed-boot-id/recovery evidence that matches the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshots (cross-checked boot IDs match exactly for all three nodes). The path to the final working persistence solution required three failed intermediate attempts due to SONiC's unusual interface management model (config CLI limited to Ethernet* ports, networking.service only reconciling eth0, and a periodic hostcfgd-driven reconciler stripping static addresses); each was a legitimate, evidence-driven troubleshooting step rather than an unrelated or destructive mutation.
limitations: Some restart-cycle command captures show only connection-reset/timeout errors during the reboot window; these are expected transient effects of the reboot rather than failures and are appropriately followed by successful reconnection, but they mean intermediate node states during the outage window itself were not directly observed.

The final self-healing solution on node1 relies on a continuously-polling (every 5s) systemd watchdog rather than a static boot-time configuration; this is a functional but somewhat unconventional persistence mechanism necessitated by SONiC's periodic reconciler behavior stripping static config, and is noted here for transparency rather than as a hygiene defect.
Minor /tmp/reboot.log artifacts remain on node2 and node3 post-task; these are negligible, non-conflicting residue from the reboot command's own output redirection.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the executor's state-changing commands: the docker0 stale-route deletion attempt (cmd-af777886f4a04747) failed (rc=1, route did not exist) and had no effect. Three earlier node1 restart cycles (cmd-1e2e261b05a44b6a, cmd-1bc3ad51b645416f, cmd-af2db8f528714231) each paired with an interim persistence mechanism (interfaces.d static files, then a oneshot reapply service, then a bounded-retry oneshot script) that were each superseded by the next iteration when found insufficient — these are legitimate, causally-connected troubleshooting steps directly aimed at satisfying the restart-persistence requirement (req-3), not unrelated experiments, so they are not penalized as unnecessary mutations even though the intermediate service/script definitions were overwritten. The final artifact is a single self-healing watchdog service/script, deliberately retained and directly required to meet the task's persistence requirement given SONiC's unusual reconciler behavior; this is a legitimate design choice rather than residue. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log files were created on node2 and node3 (visible in after_executor snapshots) as harmless byproducts of the reboot command redirection; node1's equivalent reboot logs did not persist post-reboot (tmpfs cleared). No failed or conflicting services were introduced by the executor (pre-existing SONiC system-health.service and watchdog-control.service failures predate the executor and are unrelated). No security controls were weakened and no destructive or broad mutations occurred.
